item.title: GABA (Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid)
item.description:
What Is GABA?

GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid) is the brain’s primary inhibitory neurotransmitter, found in approximately 30-40% of brain synapses. Unlike excitatory neurotransmitters like glutamate that activate neurons, GABA dampens neuronal firing, reducing the overall excitability of the nervous system.

Your body synthesizes GABA from the amino acid glutamate via the enzyme glutamate decarboxylase (GAD), which requires vitamin B6 as a cofactor. During stress, anxiety, poor sleep, or chronic stimulation (caffeine, nootropics), GABA synthesis may become insufficient, leading to nervous system hyperexcitability.

item.title: The Sleep Stack: Evidence-Based Supplements for Better Sleep
item.description:
Why a Sleep Stack?

Sleep is foundational to health, yet millions struggle with it. While pharmaceutical sleep aids have their place, they often come with side effects, dependency, and poor sleep architecture.

This evidence-based stack addresses multiple physiological pathways to sleep:

  • GABA enhancement (relaxation)
  • Body temperature regulation
  • Cortisol reduction
  • Nervous system calming

The Core Stack

1. Magnesium Glycinate (300-400 mg)

Why it works:

  • Activates GABA receptors (calming neurotransmitter)
  • Regulates the HPA axis (stress response)
  • Relaxes muscles and reduces tension
  • Most deficient mineral; deficiency causes sleep problems
